entries.94.1: When that night was over and the dawn had come, having bathed and made the offering into the fire, those two sang there everything as the sage had said before.
entries.94.2: And Kakutstha heard it, wrought by the teachers of old, of a kind of recitation never known before and adorned with singing;
entries.94.3: bound in many measures and joined with string and rhythm. And hearing it from the two boys, Raghava was filled with curiosity.
entries.94.4: Then in an interval of the rite the king, that tiger among men, called the great sages and the kings and the learned and the guildsmen;
entries.94.5: the tellers of the old tales, the knowers of words, those twice-born who were elders, and the eager best of the twice-born who knew the marks of the notes;
entries.94.6: the gandharvas who know the marks, and the guildsmen above all, those who know the foot and the syllable and the compound, and those perfected in the metres;
entries.94.7: those who know the difference of measure and instant, those who have gone far in astronomy, and the knowers of ritual and the knowers of what is to be done;
entries.94.8: the knowers of tongues and of gestures, and the guildsmen without exception; those skilled in reason and in usage, and those who reason in speech;
entries.94.9: the knowers of metre, the knowers of the old tales, those best of the twice-born who know the Veda, the knowers of painting and of measure and aphorism, and those skilled in song and dance;
entries.94.10: the knowers of the sciences, those skilled in policy, and those who awaken the meaning of the Vedanta — having gathered all these, he seated the two singers.
entries.94.11: And seeing them, all the hosts of sages and the kings of great might were as though drinking in with their eyes the king and those two singers.
entries.94.12: And they all said this to one another on every side: 'These two are like Rama, as one image rises from another.
entries.94.13: 'If they were not matted-haired and if they did not wear bark, we should find no difference between these singers and Raghava.'
entries.94.14: And as they were speaking so, those two boys of the sage began there a singing that swelled the joy of the hearers.
entries.94.15: Then a sweet music beyond human began, and all the hearers came to no satisfaction with that wealth of song.
entries.94.16: It began from the beginning with the first canto shown by Narada; and from there they sang the cantos to the twentieth.
entries.94.17: Then in the afternoon, having heard those twenty cantos, Raghava, who loved his brothers, said to his brother:
entries.94.18: 'Give swiftly eighteen thousand pieces of gold to those two great souls, Kakutstha, and whatever else they may desire.' And Kakutstha gave it swiftly to the two boys, to each apart.
entries.94.19: But Kusha and Lava would not take that gold as it was given; and those two great souls said in wonder, 'What is this for?
entries.94.20: 'We live in the forest and are content with the fruit and root of the wood. What shall we do in the forest with gold and silver?'
entries.94.21: And as those two spoke so, the hearers, filled with curiosity, and Rama with them, were all greatly astonished.
entries.94.22: And Rama of great splendour, eager to hear the source of that poem, asked those two boys of the sage:
entries.94.23: 'What is the measure of this poem? What is the standing of its great-souled maker? Who is the maker of this great poem, and where is that bull among sages?'
entries.94.24: And to Raghava as he asked, those two boys of the sage said this word:
entries.94.25: 'The venerable Valmiki is its maker, and he has come to the ordering of the sacrifice. It is by him that this whole story of yours has been shown.
entries.94.26: 'For it is composed in twenty-four thousand verses, with a hundred episodes, by that ascetic of Bhrigu's line.
entries.94.27: 'And from the beginning, king, five hundred cantos; and six books have been made here by that great soul, with the Uttara among them. By that sage, who is our teacher, your story has been made.
entries.94.28: 'And so long as there is standing and life, so long does all of it endure.
entries.94.29: 'If your mind is set upon the hearing, king and great warrior, then when you have a moment in an interval of the rite, hear it with your brothers.'
entries.94.30: And Rama said, 'Very well'; and those two, taking leave of Raghava, went gladly to the place where that bull among sages was.
entries.94.31: And Rama too, with the sages and the great-souled kings, having heard the sweetness of that song, came to the hall of the rite.
entries.94.32: And he heard it, endowed with measure and rhythm, ordered in cantos, joined with note and word, and possessed of the union of string and rhythm and articulation, sung by Kusha and Lava.
entries.95.1: Thus for many days Rama heard that most auspicious song with the sages and with the kings and the monkeys.
entries.95.2: And knowing from that song that Kusha and Lava were Sita's sons, Rama said this word in the midst of that assembly, calling by his own judgement messengers of pure conduct:
entries.95.3: 'Speak my word; go from here into the venerable one's presence.
entries.95.4: 'If she is of pure conduct and if she is free of taint, let her make her own purifying here, having asked leave of the great sage.
entries.95.5: 'And knowing the sage's will and what is in Sita's mind, if she wishes to give the proof, tell me quickly.
entries.95.6: 'Tomorrow at dawn let Maithili, the daughter of Janaka, take an oath in the midst of the assembly, for my own clearing.'
entries.95.7: Hearing that most wonderful word of Raghava, the messengers went swiftly to where that bull among sages was.
entries.95.8: And saluting that great soul, blazing and of measureless splendour, they told him Rama's words, which were gentle and sweet.
entries.95.9: And hearing what they said and knowing what was in Rama's mind, that sage of very great splendour said this word:
entries.95.10: 'So let it be; may it be well with you. As Raghava says, so shall Sita do; for the husband is the deity of a woman.'
entries.95.11: Being addressed thus by the sage, all those royal messengers came swiftly back to Raghava of great might and spoke the sage's word.
entries.95.12: Then Kakutstha, glad at hearing the word of that great soul, said to the sages gathered there and to the kings:
entries.95.13: 'Let the venerable ones with their disciples, and the lords of men with their followers, and whoever else desires it, look upon Sita's oath.'
entries.95.14: Hearing that word of the great-souled Raghava, a great sound of approval arose from all the chief among the sages.
entries.95.15: And the great-souled kings praised Raghava: 'This befits you alone upon the earth, best of men, and no other.'
entries.95.16: Having so made his resolve, that 'It shall be tomorrow,' Raghava, slayer of foes, dismissed them all then.
entries.95.17: Thus having taken counsel, that lion among kings, that great soul of great dignity, having settled the oath for the morrow, dismissed all the sages and the kings.
entries.96.1: When that night was over, the king Raghava of great splendour, having come to the sacrificial enclosure, called all the sages.
entries.96.2: Vasishtha and Vamadeva, Jabali and Kashyapa, Vishvamitra, Dirghatapas, and Durvasa of great penance;
entries.96.3: Pulastya also, and Shakti, and Bhargava and Vamana; Markandeya of long life, and Maudgalya of great renown;
entries.96.4: Garga and Chyavana, and Shatananda the knower of dharma, and Bharadvaja of splendour, and the son of Agni of fair radiance;
entries.96.5: Narada and Parvata, and Gautama of great renown, Katyayana and Suyajna, and Agastya the treasury of penance —
entries.96.6: these and many other sages of strict vows, all of them filled with curiosity, came together.
entries.96.7: And the rakshasas of great valour and the monkeys of great strength, all those great souls came out of curiosity.
entries.96.8: And kshatriyas and shudras and vaishyas by the thousand, and brahmins of strict vows come from many lands;
entries.96.9: those settled in knowledge, those settled in works, and others settled in yoga — all came together to look upon Sita's oath.
entries.96.10: Hearing that all had gathered there, unmoving as a mountain of stone, that best of sages came swiftly with Sita.
entries.96.11: And Sita followed behind that sage with her face bent down, with joined palms, her voice choked with tears, holding Rama in her mind.
entries.96.12: And seeing Sita following behind Valmiki as the Shruti follows behind Brahma, a great sound of approval arose.
entries.96.13: Then a tumult of voices went up from them all, their souls troubled by a wide grief born of sorrow.
entries.96.14: Some cried 'Well done, Rama' and others 'Well done, Sita'; and others there among the onlookers cried out upon them both.
entries.96.15: Then, entering the midst of that press of people, Valmiki the bull among sages, with Sita beside him, said this to Raghava:
entries.96.16: 'This is Sita, son of Dasharatha, of good vows and walking in dharma; abandoned because of the reproaches, she has dwelt near my hermitage.
entries.96.17: 'To you, Rama of great vows, who feared the reproach of the world, Sita will give the proof; you should give her leave.
entries.96.18: 'And these two sons of Janaki, both born together as twins, are your own sons, hard to assail. This is the truth I tell you.
entries.96.19: 'I am the tenth son of Prachetas, delight of the Raghus; I do not remember an untrue word spoken. These two are your sons.
entries.96.20: 'For many thousands of years the practice of penance has been performed by me; let me not eat the fruit of it if this Maithili is defiled.
entries.96.21: 'In mind, in deed and in word no sin has been done by me before; let me eat the fruit of that penance if Maithili is without sin.
entries.96.22: 'I, having pondered in the five elements with mind as the sixth, Raghava, took Sita by the mountain stream, knowing her to be pure.
entries.96.23: 'She is of pure conduct, without sin, and the worshipper of her husband; and to you who feared the reproach of the world she will give the proof.
entries.96.24: 'Therefore, son of the best of men, she is of pure being and came then within the range of my divine sight — she whom you abandoned, though you knew her pure, with a mind made foul by the reproach of the world, your most beloved.'
entries.97.1: Being addressed thus by Valmiki, Raghava answered with joined palms in the midst of the world, looking upon that lady of the fairest hue:
entries.97.2: 'It is even so, greatly blessed one, as you say, knower of dharma. The proof is mine, brahmin, by your untainted words.
entries.97.3: 'And the proof was given before by Vaidehi in the presence of the gods; and there an oath was taken, and by that she was brought into my house. But the reproach of the world was strong, and by that Maithili was abandoned.
entries.97.4: 'She was abandoned by me out of fear of the world, brahmin, though I knew her sinless; she should forgive that state of mind.
entries.97.5: 'And I know these two, Kusha and Lava born as twins, to be my sons. Let my joy come with Maithili proved pure in the midst of the world.'
entries.97.6: And knowing Rama's intention, those best of gods, at that oath of Sita's, Mahendra and the rest of great might,
entries.97.7: all came together, setting the Grandsire before them.
entries.97.8: The Adityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the two Ashvins with the hosts of Maruts, and the gandharvas and apsaras — all came together.
entries.97.9: The Sadhyas and the Vishvedevas and all the highest sages, the nagas and suparnas and siddhas — all of them with glad minds, eager at Sita's oath, came together.
entries.97.10: Seeing the gods and the sages, Raghava said again: 'The proof is mine, best of men, by the untainted words of the sage.
entries.97.11: 'Let my joy come with Vaidehi proved pure in the midst of the world.'
entries.97.12: Then a wind auspicious and holy, of divine fragrance and delightful, best of the gods, gladdened that press of people on every side.
entries.97.13: And the men gathered from all the kingdoms looked upon that thing, wonderful and past thought, as it had been of old in the Krita age.
entries.97.14: And seeing them all gathered, Sita, wearing an ochre robe, said this word with joined palms, her eyes cast down and her face bent low:
entries.97.15: 'As I do not think even in mind of any other than Raghava, so let the goddess Madhavi give me an opening.
entries.97.16: 'As in mind, in deed and in word I worship Rama, so let the goddess Madhavi give me an opening.
entries.97.17: 'As this that I have spoken is true, that I know none other than Rama, so let the goddess Madhavi give me an opening.'
entries.97.18: And as Vaidehi was taking that oath, a wonder appeared: a divine and unmatched throne rose up from the surface of the earth,
entries.97.19: borne upon their heads by nagas of measureless valour, divine, with divine bodies and adorned with divine jewels.
entries.97.20: And upon it the goddess Dharani took Maithili in her two arms and, greeting her with welcome, seated her upon the throne.
entries.97.21: And as she sat upon that throne and entered the nether world, an unbroken and divine rain of flowers scattered down upon Sita.
entries.97.22: And a great cry of approval rose suddenly from the gods: 'Well done, well done, Sita, whose conduct is such as this.'
entries.97.23: Thus the gods standing in the sky uttered words of many kinds with glad minds, seeing Sita's entrance.
entries.97.24: And all those sages who had come to the sacrificial enclosure, and the kings, those tigers among men, did not cease from wonder.
entries.97.25: And in the sky and upon the earth, all things moving and unmoving, and the danavas of great bulk, and the lords of serpents in the nether world —
entries.97.26: some cried out in gladness, some were sunk in meditation, some gazed upon Rama and some, past sense, upon Sita.
entries.97.27: Seeing Sita's entrance, such was the state that came upon them; for that moment the whole world alike was utterly bewildered.
entries.98.1: When Vaidehi had entered the nether world, all the monkeys cried 'Well done, virtuous one,' and the sages did the same in Rama's presence.
entries.98.2: Leaning upon his staff, his eyes troubled with tears, his head bent down and his mind wretched, Rama was in deep sorrow.
entries.98.3: Having wept a long while and shed tears again and again, Rama, filled with anger and with grief, said this word:
entries.98.4: 'My mind wishes as it were to touch a sorrow never known before, in that Sita has vanished before my eyes like Shri made visible.
entries.98.5: 'Sita passed out of sight before, beyond the great ocean in Lanka, and even from there she was brought back by me; how much more then from the face of the earth?
entries.98.6: 'Goddess Vasudha, let Sita be given back to me; or I shall show my anger, so that you shall know me.
entries.98.7: 'You are indeed my mother-in-law, for it was from you that Maithili was drawn up of old by Janaka as he ploughed with the plough in his hand.
entries.98.8: 'Therefore let Sita be given back, or give me an opening; in the nether world or in heaven, let me dwell together with her.
entries.98.9: 'Bring me that Sita; I am mad for Maithili's sake. And if you will not give me Sita in her own form upon the face of the earth,
entries.98.10: 'I shall destroy your whole standing, with your mountains and forests; I shall lay waste the earth, and let all here become water.'
entries.98.11: As Kakutstha spoke thus, filled with anger and with grief, Brahma with the hosts of the gods said to the delight of the Raghus:
entries.98.12: 'Rama, Rama, you should not grieve, one of good vows. Remember your former state and the mantra, wearer-down of foes.
entries.98.13: 'I would not remind you of that unmatched thing, mighty-armed one; but in this moment, one hard to assail, remember your birth as Vishnu.
entries.98.14: 'For Sita is spotless and virtuous and has always been devoted to you; and she has gone happily to the world of the nagas by the strength of the penance she took under your shelter.
entries.98.15: 'Your meeting with her shall be again in heaven, and there is no doubt of it. And hear what I say in the midst of this assembly.
entries.98.16: 'This very poem is yours, and it is heard as the best of poems. Valmiki will set it all forth in full, Rama, and there is no doubt.
entries.98.17: 'From your birth onward, hero, your tasting of happiness and sorrow, and what is to come hereafter — all has been made by Valmiki.
entries.98.18: 'This is the first poem, Rama, and all of it is established in you; for none but Raghava deserves to be the sharer of the glory of poems.
entries.98.19: 'This has all been heard by me before, together with the gods — divine and of wondrous form, of true speech and unveiled.
entries.98.20: 'So do you, tiger among men, being well settled in dharma, hear the rest of the poem of the Ramayana that is to come, Kakutstha.
entries.98.21: 'The rest of the poem here is called the Uttara, one of great renown; hear that highest part, one of great splendour, together with the sages.
entries.98.22: 'And this highest part is not to be heard by any other, Kakutstha; it is by the sage, hero, delight of the Raghus, that this supreme part is to be told to you alone.'
entries.98.23: Having spoken this much, Brahma the lord of the three worlds went to the third heaven with the gods and with his kinsmen.
entries.98.24: And those great-souled sages who were dwellers in the world of Brahma, having taken leave of Brahma, turned back, those of great might, being minded to hear the Uttara, what is to come in Raghava's story.
entries.98.25: Then Rama, having heard that auspicious speech uttered by the god of gods, that one of the highest splendour said this to Valmiki:
entries.98.26: 'Venerable one, the sages who dwell in the world of Brahma are minded to hear. Let that which is to come hereafter in my story begin tomorrow.'
entries.98.27: Having so resolved and taking Kusha and Lava with him, he dismissed that press of people and went to his leaf-hut; and that night passed for him as he grieved for that very Sita.
entries.99.1: When the night was over and the dawn had come, having gathered the great sages, Rama said to his two sons, 'Let it be sung without hesitation.'
entries.99.2: Then, when the great-souled brahmarshis were seated, Kusha and Lava sang that poem of what was to come.
entries.99.3: When Sita had entered the surface of the earth by the wealth of her truth, at the ending of that sacrifice Rama was in the deepest sorrow of mind.
entries.99.4: Not seeing Vaidehi, he thought this world empty; being greatly worn with grief, he came to no peace of mind.
entries.99.5: Dismissing all the kings and the bears and monkeys and rakshasas, and dismissing the press of the chief among the twice-born with wealth given first,
entries.99.6: and having thus completed the sacrifice according to the ordinance, Raghava then dismissed them all, Rama of the lotus eyes;
entries.99.7: and setting Sita in his heart he entered Ayodhya, that lord of men who had performed the sacrifice, together with his two sons.
entries.99.8: And that delight of the Raghus took no other wife beyond Sita; and at every sacrifice a golden Janaki stood for the wife.
entries.99.9: For ten thousand years he performed horse-sacrifices, and ten times as many Vajapeyas, and many rites rich in gold.
entries.99.10: With the Agnishtoma and the Atiratra and with Gosavas of great wealth, and with other rites of ample gifts, that glorious one sacrificed.
entries.99.11: Thus a very great time passed for that great soul Raghava, standing in the kingdom and striving in dharma.
entries.99.12: And day by day the bears and monkeys and rakshasas, standing within Rama's rule, gave delight to the king Raghava.
entries.99.13: The rain-god sent rain in season, food was plentiful and the quarters were clear; the city and the country were thronged with people glad and well nourished.
entries.99.14: None died out of season and there was no sickness among living creatures, and no misfortune was to be found, while Rama ruled the kingdom.
entries.99.15: Then after a long time the glorious mother of Rama, surrounded by her sons and her sons' sons, came to the law of time.
entries.99.16: And Sumitra followed after her, and the glorious Kaikeyi; and having done dharma of many kinds, they stood in the third heaven.
entries.99.17: All of them, greatly blessed, rejoicing in heaven, came together with King Dasharatha and obtained the whole fruit of dharma.
entries.99.18: And Rama gave great gifts for them from time to time, for his mothers without distinction, among the brahmins and the ascetics.
entries.99.19: And Rama, that soul of dharma, performed the rites of the fathers, and the giving of the jewels of Brahman, and sacrifices most hard to accomplish, increasing the fathers and the gods.
entries.99.20: Thus many thousands of years passed happily for him, as he increased dharma of many kinds always with sacrifices.
entries.100.1: Then after some time Yudhajit, the king of the Kekayas, sent his own teacher to the great-souled Raghava — Gargya, the son of Angiras, a brahmarshi of measureless splendour;
entries.100.2: and ten thousand horses as an unmatched gift of affection,
entries.100.3: and blankets and jewels and the finest of figured cloth; these the king gave to Rama, and auspicious ornaments.
entries.100.4: And hearing that the great sage Gargya had come, and that this great wealth had been sent by his mother's brother, the lord of horses, the wise Raghava,
entries.100.5: Kakutstha with his brothers went out a full krosha to meet him and honoured Gargya as Shakra honours Brihaspati.
entries.100.6: And having so honoured that sage and received that wealth, and asked step by step after all the welfare of his mother's brother, Rama began to question that greatly blessed one as he sat.
entries.100.7: 'What word did my mother's brother say, for which purpose your honour has come here, best of those skilled in speech, like Brihaspati made visible?'
entries.100.8: Hearing Rama's speech, the great sage began to tell Raghava the full extent of the matter, which seemed a wonder:
entries.100.9: 'Your mother's brother, mighty-armed one, that bull among men, Yudhajit, has said a word full of affection; let it be heard, if it pleases you.
entries.100.10: 'There is this land of the gandharvas, adorned with fruit and root, a region most beautiful upon both banks of the Sindhu.
entries.100.11: 'And gandharvas guard it, armed and skilled in war — three crores of them, hero, the mighty sons of Shailusha.
entries.100.12: 'Having conquered them, Kakutstha, settle that fair city of the gandharvas as your own well-ordered city, mighty-armed one.
entries.100.13: 'There is no way there for another, and the region is most beautiful. Let it please you, mighty-armed one; I do not speak to you what is not for your good.'
entries.100.14: Hearing that, Raghava was pleased with the great sage and with his mother's brother, and said only 'Very well,' and looked toward Bharata.
entries.100.15: And that Raghava, pleased, said to the twice-born one with joined palms: 'These two princes shall range in that region, brahmarshi.
entries.100.16: 'They are the sons of Bharata, the heroes Taksha and Pushkala, well guarded by their mother's brother and set with full attention in dharma.
entries.100.17: 'And setting Bharata before them, those two princes with their forces and followers shall slay the sons of the gandharvas and divide two cities between them.
entries.100.18: 'And having settled his sons in those best of cities and established them, that most righteous one shall come back again into my presence.'
entries.100.19: Having spoken thus to the brahmarshi, he then gave his command to Bharata with his forces and followers, and consecrated the two princes.
entries.100.20: And under an auspicious constellation, setting the son of Angiras before him, Bharata went out with his army and with the two princes.
entries.100.21: And that army, like an army with Shakra in it, went forth from the city; and Raghava followed it a long way — that army, hard to assail even by the gods.
entries.100.22: And flesh-eating creatures and rakshasas of very great size followed after Bharata out of a thirst for blood.
entries.100.23: And many hosts of beings, eaters of flesh and most dreadful, followed by the thousand, wishing to eat the flesh of the gandharvas' sons.
entries.100.24: And many thousands of lions and tigers and boars, and of birds that move in the sky, went before the army.
entries.100.25: And having stayed a month and a half upon the road, that army, free of sickness and thronged with people glad and well nourished, came to the Kekaya land.
entries.101.1: Hearing that Bharata had come as leader of the host, Yudhajit the lord of the Kekayas, with Gargya beside him, came to the highest joy.
entries.101.2: And the lord of the Kekayas went out with a great press of people and, making haste, marched against the gandharvas who take what form they wish.
entries.101.3: And Bharata and Yudhajit, joining with those of swift valour, came to the city of the gandharvas with their forces and followers.
entries.101.4: And hearing that Bharata had come, those gandharvas gathered, wishing to fight, and roared on every side, being of great valour.
entries.101.5: Then there was a tumultuous battle that made the hair stand on end, most dreadful, for seven nights; and there was no victory for either side.
entries.101.6: And rivers of blood with swords and spears and bows for their crocodiles, bearing the bodies of men, ran forth in every direction.
entries.101.7: Then Rama's younger brother Bharata in anger loosed against the gandharvas the most dreadful weapon of Kala, named Samvarta.
entries.101.8: And they, bound in the noose of Kala, were torn apart by the Samvarta; and in a moment three crores of those great souls were struck down by it.
entries.101.9: The dwellers in heaven do not remember such a slaughter, dreadful to look upon — that in the space of a blink such great souls should perish.
entries.101.10: And when all of them were slain, Bharata the son of Kaikeyi settled two flourishing and excellent cities.
entries.101.11: Taksha in Takshashila and Pushkala in Pushkalavata, in that lovely land of the gandharvas and in the country of Gandhara;
entries.101.12: strewn with heaps of wealth and jewels and adorned with woods, made to vie with one another in rivalry through the extent of their virtues.
entries.101.13: Both of shining beauty, with dealings free of taint, filled with gardens and carriages and with markets well laid out between;
entries.101.14: both those best of cities lovely and adorned in their extent, with fair chief houses of the colour of celestial cars;
entries.101.15: adorned with fine and spreading temples of the gods, and adorned with palmyras and tamalas, with tilakas and bakulas.
entries.101.16: Having settled them in five years, Bharata, the mighty-armed son of Kaikeyi and younger brother of Raghava, came again to Ayodhya.
entries.101.17: And the glorious Bharata saluted that great soul Raghava, who was as a second Dharma made visible, as Vasava salutes Brahma.
entries.101.18: And he told as it had happened that excellent slaying of the gandharvas and the settling of the country; and Raghava was pleased to hear it.
entries.102.1: Hearing that, Raghava with his brothers came to gladness, and said then to Lakshmana a word of wondrous seeming:
entries.102.2: 'These two princes, Saumitri, are skilled in dharma and firm of valour for a kingdom — Angada and Chandraketu.
entries.102.3: 'I shall consecrate these two in a kingdom; let a good country be found, lovely and unconfined, where those two bowmen may take their pleasure.
entries.102.4: 'Where there is no affliction to a king and no destruction of hermitages — let such a country be seen, gentle one, so that we do no wrong.'
entries.102.5: As Rama spoke thus, Bharata answered: 'This land of Karupatha is lovely and free of ill.
entries.102.6: 'Let a city for the great-souled Angada be settled there, and for Chandraketu the shining and unafflicted Chandrakanta.'
entries.102.7: Raghava accepted that word spoken by Bharata; and having brought that country under his sway, he settled Angada there.
entries.102.8: And Angada's city, called Angadiya, was settled and made lovely and well guarded by Rama, whose deeds are done without effort.
entries.102.9: And Chandraketu's city was settled in the Malla land, renowned as Chandrakanta, divine as the city of heaven.
entries.102.10: Then Rama and Lakshmana and Bharata, hard to assail in battle, came to the highest joy and performed the consecration.
entries.102.11: And having consecrated the two princes, Raghava sent them forth — Angada to the western land and Chandraketu with his face to the north.
entries.102.12: And Saumitri Lakshmana followed after Angada, and Bharata became the rear-guard of Chandraketu.
entries.102.13: And Lakshmana dwelt a year in Angadiya, and when his son was firmly settled, hard to assail, he came again to Ayodhya.
entries.102.14: And Bharata too, having dwelt somewhat more than a year, came again to Ayodhya and waited upon Rama's feet.
entries.102.15: And those two, Saumitri and Bharata, devoted to Rama's feet, most righteous, did not know the time that passed, for love.
entries.102.16: Thus ten thousand years went by for them, as they strove always in dharma in the affairs of the citizens.
entries.102.17: Having passed that time with their hearts fulfilled, encircled by fortune and well established in the city of dharma, they shone as three kindled fires of blazing splendour well offered in a great sacrifice.
entries.103.1: Then after some time, while Rama stood devoted to dharma, Kala came to the door of the royal house in the form of an ascetic.
entries.103.2: And he said this word to Lakshmana, the steadfast and glorious: 'Announce me to Rama; I have come upon a weighty matter.
entries.103.3: 'I am the messenger of a great sage of exceeding strength and measureless might; I have come wishing to see Rama upon a business, one of great strength.'
entries.103.4: Hearing that word of his, Saumitri went with haste and announced to Rama that ascetic who had come:
entries.103.5: 'Conquer both worlds by dharma, Rama of great splendour. A messenger has come to see you, bright as the sun with penance.'
entries.103.6: Hearing that word spoken by Lakshmana, Rama said: 'Let that sage of great might be brought in, dear one, who bears his word.'
entries.103.7: And Saumitri said 'Even so' and brought that sage in, blazing with splendour and as though burning with his rays.
entries.103.8: And coming to that best of the Raghus, who shone with his own splendour, the sage said to Raghava in a sweet voice, 'May you prosper.'
entries.103.9: And Rama of great splendour gave him honour with the guest-offering first, and began without haste to ask after his welfare.
entries.103.10: And being asked after his welfare by Rama, that greatly renowned one, best of speakers, sat down upon a divine seat of gold.
entries.103.11: Then Rama said to him: 'Welcome to you, great sage. Deliver the words of him from whom you have come as messenger.'
entries.103.12: Being urged by that lion among kings, the sage spoke this word: 'This is to be told between us two alone, if you have regard for your own good.
entries.103.13: 'Whoever hears it or looks upon it shall become fit to be slain by you — so it must be, if you have regard for the word of that chief among sages.'
entries.103.14: And Rama, promising 'Even so,' said to Lakshmana: 'Stand at the door, mighty-armed one, and dismiss the doorkeeper.
entries.103.15: 'Whoever should see or hear the talk that passes between the sage and me shall certainly be fit to be slain by me, Saumitri.'
entries.103.16: Then Kakutstha, having set Lakshmana at the door to keep it, said to him, 'Speak your word, sage.'
entries.103.17: 'Whatever word is in your mind, or with whatever you are charged — tell it without hesitation; it shall rest in my heart.'
entries.104.1: 'Hear, king of great courage, for what I have come. I have been sent by the god and Grandsire, one of great strength.
entries.104.2: 'In your former being I was your son, conqueror of the cities of your foes — brought forth by your maya, hero: Kala, the gatherer of all.
entries.104.3: 'And the venerable Grandsire, lord and master of the worlds, has said: "The term you appointed, gentle one, for the guarding of the worlds, is fulfilled.
entries.104.4: '"For having gathered up the worlds of old by your own maya, lying upon the water in the great ocean, you brought me forth before.
entries.104.5: '"And then, by your maya, the serpent Ananta with his hoods, lying upon the water, and two beings of great strength —
entries.104.6: '"Madhu and Kaitabha, with whose heaps of bones this earth, thronged with mountains, became the ground we tread.
entries.104.7: '"And having brought me forth too from your navel upon a divine lotus bright as the sun, you set the whole work of Prajapati upon me.
entries.104.8: '"And I, laid down of my burden, worship you the lord of the world. Appoint the guarding among created beings; you are the maker of my splendour.
entries.104.9: '"Then you also, out of that eternal state hard to assail, came to the state of Vishnu for the guarding of all beings.
entries.104.10: '"A valiant son of Aditi and the increaser of the valour of your brothers, you were fit to be their help when tasks arose.
entries.104.11: '"And when the people were terrified, best in the worlds, wishing the death of Ravana, you set your mind among men.
entries.104.12: '"Ten thousand years and ten hundreds of years — having yourself of old appointed by your own act the fixed term of your dwelling —
entries.104.13: '"you, that son born of the mind, have your full term among men here; and this, best of men, is the hour for you to come near.
entries.104.14: '"If, great king, you wish yet again that the people should wait upon you, then dwell, hero, and may it be well with you." So says the Grandsire.
entries.104.15: '"Or if you have the will to conquer for the world of the gods, Raghava, let the gods have Vishnu as their protector and be free of fever."'
entries.104.16: Hearing the word of the Grandsire uttered by Kala, Raghava laughing said this word to the gatherer of all:
entries.104.17: 'Hearing this most wonderful word of the god of gods, a great joy has arisen in me at your coming.
entries.104.18: 'My coming to be was for the sake of the three worlds. May it be well with you; I shall go to that from which I came.
entries.104.19: 'You have come to what is already in my heart, and I have no debate about it. For in all the works of the gods, who follow their own will, I must stand, gatherer of all, as the Grandsire says.'
entries.105.1: As those two were speaking so, the venerable sage Durvasa, wishing to see Rama, came to the door of the royal house.
entries.105.2: And coming to Saumitri, that best of sages said: 'Show me Rama swiftly, before my purpose is overpassed.'
entries.105.3: Hearing the sage's word, Lakshmana, slayer of enemy heroes, saluted that great soul and said this word:
entries.105.4: 'What is to be done, venerable one? Tell me. What is the matter, and what shall I do? Raghava is engaged, brahmin; let there be waiting for a moment.'
entries.105.5: Hearing that, that tiger among sages, made foul with anger, said this word to Lakshmana, as though burning him with his eye:
entries.105.6: 'In this very moment announce me to Rama, Saumitri. If in this very moment you do not announce me, Saumitri,
entries.105.7: 'I shall curse you and the realm and the city and Raghava too, and Bharata as well, Saumitri, and whatever offspring is yours.
entries.105.8: 'For I shall not be able to hold this wrath in my heart any longer.' Hearing that word of that great soul, dreadful to seeming, he pondered in mind the certainty of that word.
entries.105.9: 'Let there be the death of one, and not the destruction of all.' Having so settled it by his judgement, he announced him to Raghava.
entries.105.10: Hearing Lakshmana's word, Rama dismissed Kala and came out swiftly, and that king looked upon the son of Atri.
entries.105.11: Saluting that great soul, blazing as it were with splendour, Kakutstha said with joined palms, 'What is to be done?'
entries.105.12: Hearing that word spoken by Raghava, that best of sages, Durvasa, answered that lord Rama: 'Let it be heard, lover of dharma.
entries.105.13: 'Today the completion of my penance of a thousand years has come. So I wish for food, sinless one, such as is ready with you.'
entries.105.14: Hearing that word, the king Raghava with a pleased mind brought food such as was ready to that chief among sages.
entries.105.15: And that best of sages, having eaten that food which was like nectar, said 'Well done, Rama,' and went to his own hermitage.
entries.105.16: When that best of sages had gone to his own hermitage, the elder brother of Lakshmana remembered Kala's words and came then to sorrow.
entries.105.17: And being greatly burnt with sorrow, remembering that dreadful thing, with his face bent down and his mind wretched, he could not speak.
entries.105.18: Then, having settled Kala's words by his judgement and concluded that there was no help for it, that greatly renowned one sat silent.
entries.106.1: Then, seeing Raghava with his face bent down and wretched, like the moon steeped in water, Lakshmana gladly said this sweet word:
entries.106.2: 'You should not grieve for my sake, mighty-armed one; for the course of Kala is bound thus by what was ordained before.
entries.106.3: 'Slay me without hesitation, gentle one, and keep your promise. Men fallen from their promise go to hell, Kakutstha.
entries.106.4: 'If there is affection in you, great king, and if there is favour toward me, slay me without hesitation and increase dharma, Raghava.'
entries.106.5: Being addressed thus by Lakshmana, Rama, his senses shaken, gathered his ministers and the household priest as well.
entries.106.6: And Raghava told in their midst all that had happened — the coming of Durvasa and the promise of the ascetic.
entries.106.7: Hearing that, all the ministers with the teachers sat silent; and Vasishtha of great splendour said this word:
entries.106.8: 'This wasting of yours that makes the hair stand on end has been foreseen, mighty-armed one, and this parting from Lakshmana, Rama of great renown.
entries.106.9: 'Abandon him; Kala is strong. Do not make your promise vain. When a promise is destroyed, dharma too will go to dissolution.
entries.106.10: 'And then, when dharma is destroyed, the three worlds with all that moves and does not move, with the gods and the hosts of sages, would be destroyed; there is no doubt.
entries.106.11: 'So do you, tiger among men, for the guarding of the three worlds, make the world well today, even without Lakshmana.'
entries.106.12: Hearing that word of theirs, gathered there and joined with dharma and with what is right, Rama said to Lakshmana in the midst of the assembly:
entries.106.13: 'I dismiss you, Saumitri; let there be no overturning of dharma. For the good, both abandonment and slaying are appointed alike.'
entries.106.14: When that word was spoken by Rama, Lakshmana, his senses troubled with tears, went swiftly and did not enter his own house.
entries.106.15: And going to the bank of the Sarayu and touching the water, with joined palms, he restrained all his currents and did not let go his breath.
entries.106.16: And seeing him breathless and joined in yoga, the gods with Shakra and with the hosts of apsaras, and all with the hosts of sages, scattered flowers upon him then.
entries.106.17: And unseen by all men, Shakra took Lakshmana of great strength in his body and entered the third heaven.
entries.106.18: Then, seeing the fourth part of Vishnu come, all those best of gods with the great sages, being glad, did him honour.
entries.107.1: Having dismissed Lakshmana, Rama, filled with sorrow and grief, said this to the household priest and the ministers and the guildsmen:
entries.107.2: 'Today I shall consecrate in the kingdom Bharata, the lover of dharma, as the heroic lord of Ayodhya; and then I shall go to the forest.
entries.107.3: 'Bring in the materials; let there be no passing of the hour. This very day I shall go by the way that Lakshmana has gone.'
entries.107.4: Hearing that spoken by Raghava, all the people bowed their heads deeply to the ground and became as though bereft of life.
entries.107.5: And Bharata too lost his senses at hearing Rama's speech; he reproached the kingdom and said this to Raghava:
entries.107.6: 'By truth I swear it, king: not even in the world of heaven, and not the kingdom either, do I desire without you, delight of the Raghus.
entries.107.7: 'Consecrate these two, Kusha and Lava, lord of men — the hero Kusha among the Kosalas and Lava among the northern people.
entries.107.8: 'And let messengers of swift valour go to Shatrughna; let them tell him without delay of this going of ours to heaven.'
entries.107.9: Hearing that spoken by Bharata, and seeing the citizens with their faces bent down and burnt with sorrow, Vasishtha said this word:
entries.107.10: 'Child Rama, see these people gone to the earth. Knowing the thing they desire, do not do what displeases them.'
entries.107.11: And at Vasishtha's word, having raised the people up, Kakutstha said to them all, 'What shall I do?'
entries.107.12: Then all the people said this word to Rama: 'We shall follow after you as you go, Rama, wherever you shall go.
entries.107.13: 'If there is affection in you for the citizens, and if there is unmatched love, let us come with our sons and wives, Kakutstha, upon that good path.
entries.107.14: 'Whether a penance-grove or a stronghold, a river or the treasury of waters — if we are not to be abandoned by you, lead us all, lord.
entries.107.15: 'This is our highest joy and this our highest boon; our joy is always in our hearts in the following of you, king.'
entries.107.16: And seeing the firm devotion of the citizens, he said only 'Very well'; and looking upon his own end, Raghava on that day
entries.107.17: consecrated both those great souls, Kusha and Lava — the hero Kusha among the Kosalas and Lava among the northern people.
entries.107.18: And having set his consecrated sons upon his lap and established them each in his city, that mighty-armed one embraced them and smelt their heads again and again.
entries.107.19: And he gave to each of them thousands of chariots and ten thousands of elephants and ten times ten thousand horses for their wealth.
entries.107.20: And rich in jewels and rich in wealth, surrounded by people glad and well nourished, he sent those two brothers Kusha and Lava each to his own city.
entries.107.21: Having consecrated his two heroic sons and established them in their cities, he then sent messengers to the great-souled Shatrughna.
entries.108.1: Those messengers of swift valour, urged by Rama's word, went quickly to Mathura and made no halt upon the road.
entries.108.2: And in three days and nights they reached Mathura and told Shatrughna all of it as it truly was —
entries.108.3: the abandonment of Lakshmana and the promise of Raghava, the consecration of the sons and the following of the citizens.
entries.108.4: 'The lovely city of Kusha upon the slope of the Vindhya mountain has been made by the wise Rama under the name Kushavati; and the lovely city Shravasti has been proclaimed for Lava.
entries.108.5: 'And having made Ayodhya empty of people, Raghava and Bharata, those two great warriors, have made their preparation for the going to heaven.'
entries.108.6: Having thus swiftly declared everything to the great-souled Shatrughna, those messengers fell silent and said, 'Make haste, king.'
entries.108.7: Hearing of that destruction of his line come upon him, dreadful to seeming, he gathered the people and the household priest Kanchana,
entries.108.8: and that delight of the Raghus told them all of it as it had happened, and his own passing with his brothers, which was to come.
entries.108.9: Then that heroic lord of men consecrated his two sons: Subahu received Mathura and Shatrughati Vaidisha.
entries.108.10: And having divided that army of Mathura in two for his two sons, and having settled wealth as was fitting, that king established them.
entries.108.11: And having set Subahu in Mathura and Shatrughati in Vaidisha, Raghava then went to Ayodhya with a single chariot.
entries.108.12: And there he saw that great soul blazing like the fire, wearing a fine linen garment, together with the imperishable sages.
entries.108.13: And saluting Rama with joined palms and his senses restrained, he spoke this word to the knower of dharma, thinking upon dharma alone:
entries.108.14: 'Having made the consecration of my two sons, delight of the line of the Raghus, know me, king, as resolved upon following you.
entries.108.15: 'And nothing else is to be said in answer, hero, nor any command. I wish this to be seen as fitting, and especially for one like me.'
entries.108.16: Knowing that unweak resolve of his, the delight of the Raghus, Rama, said only 'Very well' to Shatrughna.
entries.108.17: At the end of that word, the monkeys who take what form they wish and the hosts of bears and rakshasas came in many companies.
entries.108.18: Setting Sugriva before them, all of them came together, being minded to see that Rama who stood facing toward heaven.
entries.108.19: And the sons of the gods and the sons of the sages and the sons of the gandharvas, knowing of Rama's passing, all came together.
entries.108.20: And all those monkeys and rakshasas saluted Rama and said: 'We have come resolved upon following you, king.
entries.108.21: 'If you should go without us, Rama, best of men, then it is as though you had raised the rod of Yama and struck us down.'
entries.108.22: Being addressed thus by them, Kakutstha smiled and said, 'Very well.'
entries.108.23: In this interval Sugriva of great strength also, having saluted that hero in due form, made ready to declare himself:
entries.108.24: 'Having consecrated the hero Angada, I have come, lord of men. Know me, king, as resolved upon following you.'
entries.108.25: Hearing that word of his, Rama, best of those who take delight, said then to the lord of monkeys, thinking upon his friendship:
entries.108.26: 'Hear, friend Sugriva: I shall not go without you, whether to the world of the gods or to that supreme and great abode.'
entries.108.27: Then that greatly renowned one said to Vibhishana the lord of rakshasas: 'So long as the people shall endure, so long shall you, Vibhishana, lord of rakshasas of great valour, endure, standing in Lanka.
entries.108.28: 'So long as the moon and the sun endure, so long as the earth stands, and so long as my story is in the world, so long let your kingdom be here.
entries.108.29: 'You have been instructed in friendship, and my command is to be done by you. Guard the people in dharma; you should not answer.
entries.108.30: 'And I wish to say one thing more, lord of rakshasas of great mind:
entries.108.31: 'worship the lord of the world, the deity of the Ikshvaku line, who is to be worshipped without ceasing by all the gods with Vasava.'
entries.108.32: And Vibhishana accepted Rama's word saying 'Even so,' that king of the chief among rakshasas, remembering Raghava's command.
entries.108.33: Having spoken thus to him, Kakutstha then said to Hanuman: 'You have resolved upon living; do not break your promise.
entries.108.34: 'So long as my stories shall go about in the world, lord of monkeys, so long take your pleasure, well pleased, keeping my word.'
entries.108.35: Being addressed thus by the great-souled Raghava, Hanuman, having gained the highest joy, declared this word:
entries.108.36: 'So long as your purifying story shall move in the world, so long shall I stand upon the earth, keeping your command.'
entries.108.37: And having spoken so to Jambavan, the aged son of Brahma, and to Mainda and Dvivida — these five together with Jambavan —
entries.108.38: having spoken thus to them and to all those bears and monkeys, Kakutstha said: 'Very well; come with me as you desire.'
entries.109.1: When the night had brightened into dawn, Rama of the broad chest and great renown, whose eyes were lotus petals, said to the household priest:
entries.109.2: 'Let the blazing fire of the oblation go before with the twice-born, and the parasol of the Vajapeya shining upon the great road.'
entries.109.3: Then Vasishtha of great splendour performed in due form and without omission the whole rite of dharma for the great departure.
entries.109.4: Then, wearing a fine garment and turning over the supreme Brahman, taking kusha grass in his two hands, he went forth.
entries.109.5: Speaking nothing at all anywhere, without motion and without pleasure upon the road, he went out from that house blazing like the sun.
entries.109.6: At Rama's right side was Shri with her lotus, taking her stand, and at his left the great goddess Hri, and Resolve before him.
entries.109.7: And arrows of many kinds, and the long and excellent bow, and all his weapons went with him in the form of men.
entries.109.8: The Vedas in the form of brahmins, and Gayatri the guardian of all, and Omkara and Vashatkara — all followed after Rama.
entries.109.9: And the great-souled sages and all the gods of the earth followed after that great soul, for whom the gate of heaven stood open.
entries.109.10: And the women of the inner apartments followed him as he went, with the aged and the children and the maidservants, with the eunuchs and the attendants.
entries.109.11: And Bharata went with his inner apartments, together with Shatrughna, following the path Rama took, devoted to him, with the sacrificial fire.
entries.109.12: And all those great souls came together with their fires, and with their sons and wives followed after Kakutstha of great mind.
entries.109.13: And the ministers and the households of servants, with their sons and cattle and kinsmen, all with their followers, went after Rama as though rejoicing.
entries.109.14: Then all the people, thronged with those glad and well nourished, followed after Raghava as he went, being coloured by his virtues.
entries.109.15: Then with their women and their men, with their birds and beasts and vehicles, all the followers of Raghava were glad and free of taint.
entries.109.16: Bathed and delighted, all the monkeys were glad and well nourished, all devoted to Rama with their strong cries of joy.
entries.109.17: And there was none there wretched or ashamed or sorrowful; everything was glad and rejoicing, a thing of the highest wonder.
entries.109.18: And whoever of the country people came desiring to see Rama as he went out, he too, at the mere sight of him, followed after him gladly toward heaven.
entries.109.19: And the bears and monkeys and rakshasas and the people who dwelt in the city came behind with the highest devotion and with full attention.
entries.109.20: And whatever beings were in the city, and those that had passed out of sight, they too followed Raghava as he stood ready for heaven.
entries.109.21: And whatever things unmoving and moving looked upon Kakutstha, all of them too followed after Rama as he went.
entries.109.22: Nothing in Ayodhya was to be seen that breathed, not the least thing; and even those born in the animal kind were all devoted to Rama.
entries.110.1: Having gone a yojana and a half, the delight of the Raghus saw the river of holy waters, the Sarayu, that turns toward the west.
entries.110.2: Following that river with its whirling eddies everywhere, that king Rama, delight of the Raghus, came with his people to that place.
entries.110.3: Then in that same moment Brahma, the Grandsire of the worlds, surrounded by all the gods and by the great-souled sages,
entries.110.4: came to where Kakutstha stood ready for heaven, encircled by a hundred crores of divine celestial cars.
entries.110.5: The sky was covered with divine splendour and became an unmatched thing of light, self-shining by the splendour of those dwellers in heaven whose deeds are holy.
entries.110.6: And winds blew holy and fragrant and giving ease; and a rain of flowers loosed by the gods fell like a great flood.
entries.110.7: And in that place strewn with hundreds of drums and thronged with gandharvas and apsaras, Rama went down on foot into the water of the Sarayu.
entries.110.8: Then the Grandsire spoke a voice from the sky: 'Come, Vishnu; may it be well with you. By good fortune you have come, Raghava.
entries.110.9: 'Enter your own body with your godlike brothers. Enter what body you wish, mighty-armed one, your own — that Vaishnava splendour, one of great splendour, or that eternal space.
entries.110.10: 'For you are the way of the worlds, god, and none knows you save that wide-eyed Maya who was your consort of old. You are unthinkable, the great being, imperishable, the gatherer of all.
entries.110.11: 'Enter yourself, one of great splendour, what body you wish.'
entries.110.12: Hearing the Grandsire's word and resolving, that one of great mind entered the Vaishnava splendour in his body, together with his younger brothers.
entries.110.13: Then the gods worshipped that god who had become Vishnu — the Sadhyas and the hosts of Maruts, with Indra and with Agni at their head.
entries.110.14: And the divine hosts of sages, and the gandharvas and the apsaras, the suparnas and nagas and yakshas, the daityas and danavas and rakshasas.
entries.110.15: Everything was nourished and delighted, its desire wholly fulfilled; and by those gods came 'Well done, well done,' and heaven was free of taint.
entries.110.16: Then Vishnu of great splendour said to the Grandsire: 'You should give a world to this press of people, one of good vows.
entries.110.17: 'For all these glorious ones have followed me out of love; they are my devotees and to be cherished, and they have given up themselves for my sake.'
entries.110.18: Hearing that word of Vishnu, Brahma the lord and teacher of the worlds said: 'These who have come together shall go to the worlds called Santanika;
entries.110.19: 'and whatever creature of the animal kind shall give up its life in devotion, thinking upon you thus, it shall dwell in that Santana,
entries.110.20: 'which is joined with all the qualities of Brahman and is next after the world of Brahma.'
entries.110.21: And the monkeys and the bears went to their own origins, to those gods from whom they had all come forth, being born of the gods.
entries.110.22: And among them Sugriva entered the disc of the sun; and before the eyes of all the gods they came each to his own father.
entries.110.23: When the lord of the gods had spoken so, they came to the Gopratara, and all went into the Sarayu, overcome with tears of joy.
entries.110.24: And whatever creature went down into that water in gladness, casting off the human body, it mounted a celestial car.
entries.110.25: And hundreds of those born in the animal kind, coming to the water of the Sarayu, went to the third heaven with bodies of shining light; and divine, with divine bodies, they became as gods ablaze.
entries.110.26: And going to the water of the Sarayu, things unmoving and moving, at the touch of that water came to the world of the gods.
entries.110.27: And the bears and monkeys and rakshasas who came there too entered heaven, laying down their bodies in the water.
entries.110.28: Then, having established in heaven all who had come, the teacher of the worlds went with the ever-glad thirty to that great heaven.
entries.111.1: Such is this narrative with the Uttara, honoured by Brahma, renowned as the Ramayana, foremost, made by Valmiki.
entries.111.2: Then Vishnu was established in the world of heaven as before, by whom this whole three-fold world with all that moves and does not move is pervaded.
entries.111.3: And from that time the gods with the gandharvas, and the siddhas and the highest sages, hear always with content that divine Ramayana in heaven.
entries.111.4: This narrative gives long life and good fortune and destroys sin; the Ramayana is the equal of the Veda, and the wise should have it recited at the rites for the dead.
entries.111.5: He who is without a son obtains a son and he who is without wealth obtains wealth; and he is released from all sins who reads even a single line of it.
entries.111.6: And the man who does sins day after day, if he reads even a single verse, is released from that sin.
entries.111.7: And to the reciter should be given a garment, a cow and gold; and when the reciter is well pleased, all the gods are pleased.
entries.111.8: The man who reads this narrative, the Ramayana, which gives long life, is magnified in this world with his sons and grandsons, and after death as well.
entries.111.9: And the lovely city of Ayodhya, empty for many years, shall come to be inhabited when it has gained a king named Rishabha.
entries.111.10: This narrative which gives long life, with what is to come and with the Uttara, was made by the son of Prachetas, and Brahma too approved it.
entries.111.11: A man obtains from the mere hearing of a single canto the fruit of a thousand horse-sacrifices and of ten thousand Vajapeyas.
entries.111.12: Prayaga and the other holy fords, Ganga and the other rivers, Naimisha and the other forests, and Kurukshetra and the rest — all these have been gone to in this world by him who has heard the Ramayana.
entries.111.13: He who gives a weight of gold at Kurukshetra when the sun is eclipsed, and he who hears the Ramayana in the world — these two are alike.
entries.111.14: He who, joined with full faith, hears the story of Raghava is released from all sin and goes to the world of Vishnu.
entries.111.15: This is the first poem and holy, made of old by Valmiki; he who hears it always with devotion shall go to the Vaishnava body.
entries.111.16: And his sons and wives increase, and his wealth and his offspring. Knowing this to be true, it should be heard by those of restrained soul.
entries.111.17: And that unmatched Ramayana is the very form of the Gayatri.
entries.111.18: He who is without a son obtains a son and he who is without wealth obtains wealth; and he is released from all sins who reads even a single line of it.
entries.111.19: He who reads or hears always the story of Raghava, becoming free of taint through devotion, shall obtain long life.
entries.111.20: Let him who wishes to attain the good think always upon Raghava, and have this narrative recited to brahmins day by day.
entries.111.21: And he who reads this whole story of the lord of the Raghus goes at the wasting of his life to the world of Vishnu, and there is no doubt.
entries.111.22: His father and his father's father, and likewise his great-grandfather, and his father and his father too, go to Vishnu, and there is no doubt.
entries.111.23: The story of Raghava gives always the four ends of man; therefore with effort it should always be heard as the highest thing.
entries.111.24: He who with devotion hears of the Ramayana even a quarter or a single line goes to the abode of Brahma and is honoured always by Brahma.
entries.111.25: Thus is this narrative of what came to pass of old; may it be well with you. Recite it with confidence, and let the strength of Vishnu increase.
entries.111.26: Thus ends the hundred and eleventh canto of the Uttara Kanda in the Ramayana, the first poem of the sage Valmiki, the collection of twenty-four thousand verses.
entries.111.27: Here the Uttara Kanda is completed.
entries.111.28: Here the Ramayana, the first poem of the sage Valmiki, is complete.
entries.111.29: Let this be an offering to Sita and Ramachandra.
